title: Ingress/Egress proportional bundles with burst-credit pilot for hosted API
creator: Sophia Kim
description:
Summary:

This ticket proposes a controlled pilot that evaluates per-token directional pricing bundled into proportional ingress/egress packages with an attached burst-credit mechanism for short-lived streaming spikes. The hypothesis is that for conversational workloads with asymmetric token flows (short prompts, long outputs or vice versa), packaging directional token allowances plus a small burst credit buffer will: 1) reduce sticker shock for enterprise buyers on contracts, 2) improve predictability for heavy-output applications by smoothing bill variance, and 3) increase committed ARR via clearer enterprise commit options compared to simple symmetric per-token pricing.

Why this is different:
- Most current experiments focus on per-direction floors or streaming minimums alone. This pilot combines proportional bundles (fixed ratio of ingress:egress allocations) with transient burst credits and tests session-level smoothing windows rather than rigid monthly minimums.

Hypotheses to test:
- H1 (Commercial): A bundle that sets a 1:3 ingress:egress allocation priced at a blended discount vs pure per-token will lift committed conversion rates in pilot enterprise contracts by >=10% vs baseline offers.
- H2 (Behavioral): Developers will prefer an explicit burst buffer for ephemeral peaks rather than purchasing a larger permanent commit.
- H3 (Revenue): Net revenue per customer will not decline more than 2% while average perceived predictability improves (qualitative surveys).

Experiment design:
- Population: 50 pilot customers (mix of mid-market SaaS & AI-native startups) recruited from existing contract renewal pipeline and outbound pilot invites.
- Variants: 
  - Control: Current symmetric per-token pricing (Ingress/Output same rate) + current streaming minimums.
  - Variant A: Proportional bundle (1:3 ingress:egress) with blended per-token price (5% discount vs Control) + burst-credit of 20% of monthly commit usable across sessions with 24-hour decay.
  - Variant B: Proportional bundle (1:2 ingress:egress) with blended price (3% discount) + burst-credit 10% with 72-hour decay and session-window smoothing.
- Allocation: Randomized by customer cohort where contractual constraints allow; otherwise matched pair assignment.
- Duration: 90 days active pilot + 30 day follow-up.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Primary metric: Conversion to reserved commitment (signed monthly/annual) during pilot (target +10% relative lift for either variant vs Control).
- Secondary metrics: Average monthly revenue per customer, churn rate over 6 months after pilot (target delta <=2%), median billing variance (month-to-month) reduced by >=15% for bundle customers, customer-reported predictability score (+0.5 NPS-like scale).
- Safety gates: If any pilot customer sees >15% unexpected invoice spike vs forecast in any month, pause rollout and investigate.

Telemetry and analysis plan:
- Query 1 (baseline usage patterns): BigQuery: SELECT customer_id, SUM(input_tokens) AS in_tok, SUM(output_tokens) AS out_tok, COUNT(session_id) FROM `billing.hosted_token_usage` WHERE date BETWEEN @start AND @end GROUP BY customer_id; used to identify asymmetric workloads.
- Query 2 (billing variance): Snowflake: monthly invoice totals grouped over 12 months for pilot vs matched controls.
- Dashboard: experimentation dashboard (Looker) created: dashboards/pricing/pilots/pm-552341-bundle-burst.
- Statistical tests: Bootstrap revenue lift CI; 90% power to detect a 10% lift in conversions with 50 customers (verify with uplift calculator).

Billing rules and contract language (draft summary):
- Bundle defined as X ingress tokens + Y egress tokens per month. Overages billed at tiered per-token rates (higher than committed unit).
- Burst credit: short-lived token allowance that draws against a separate bucket; when exhausted, overage rates apply. Burst credits expire per policy (24h or 72h depending on variant).
- Visibility: Console to show remaining bundle allocation, burst buffer, and projected burn rate at session level.

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Metering: ENG must add burst credit bucket to billing pipeline and expose per-session remaining credit via token-usage endpoints. Associated GH work: github.com/redwood-inference/pricing/PR#5234 (metering bridge), PR#5310 (console UI).
- Runtime: Serving runtime changes limited; no model-side enforcement required; enforcement in gateway + billing pipeline.
- Rollout safety: start with read-only simulation mode for first 14 days to verify telemetry before actually billing through new constructs.

Customer communications and sales playbook:
- Create one-pager for sales explaining bundle math, sample contract language, and positioning vs traditional monthly minimums. Link: confluence.redwood.ai/pricing/pm-552341-bundle-playbook.
- CS onboarding checklist for pilot customers and billing FAQ.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Complexity causes confusion and slows sales cycles. Mitigation: Strict sales playbook + tooling in console summarizing cost impact and examples.
- Risk: Edge cases where long-running streaming sessions consume burst credits quickly, causing surprise overage. Mitigation: Session-level alerts and initial simulation mode.
- Risk: Accounting/recognition complexity for blend discounts. Mitigation: Finance to sign off on revenue recognition approach before first invoice.

Deliverables:
- Experiment spec and signed pilot recruit list (PM).
- Metering + billing pipeline changes merged behind a feature flag (ENG).
- Console UX to display bundle & burst status (DES + ENG).
- Analytical dashboard and queries (PM + Analytics).
- Sales one-pager and contract appendix language (PM + Legal).

Acceptance criteria for finishing ticket:
1) Pilot plan document approved by Revenue Ops and Legal.
2) Metering simulation runs for 14 days with no >5% discrepancy vs ground truth billing.
3) Console surfaces bundle/burst data for pilot customers.
4) Experiment dashboard populated and initial cohort assigned.
